question.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=x\,i-z\,j+y\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2,\,y=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i-z\,j+y\,k \\  & =2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,k \\  & =0\,i-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k) \\  & =2\cdot 0+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\pi \,\text{d}t \\  & =\pi [t]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi (2-0) \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$
